title: Rank 1. The store screenshots do not show what Pexi does: the first one is an empty camera, none has a caption, none shows a Great or Bad price verdict
evidence: Viewed docs/store/screenshots/iphone-6.9/01-camera.png: blurred viewfinder, corner brackets, mascot bubble 'Point at a barcode.' 02-cheerios.png and 03-butterlist.png: a price range ('$5.45 to $11.80, Based on 5 sellers') and a 'Tell me the price' button, no verdict. No image has a headline caption. 04-search and 05-you not opened (names only, assumed). iphone-6.3/06-paywall.png (dated 2026-11-09, before build 10's paywall changes) shows the subscribe screen, which sells nothing to a browser.
fix: Replace the set with 4 or 5 captioned frames, first one a big verdict on a familiar item (e.g. butter at a real shelf price, 'Great price') with a caption like 'Scan it. Know if it is a good price.'; second the range chart with 'See what it usually costs in Canada'; drop the paywall frame. No savings figure in any caption (hard rule 2).
fix_cost: 3 to 4 hours (Aurik owns screenshots per RULINGS 'Who owns what'), $0

title: Rank 2. The App Store name is just 'Pexi', so the strongest search field carries no words a shopper types
evidence: docs/store/listing.md:7 '**Name:** Pexi' (4 of 30 characters). Subtitle listing.md:12 'Is this price a good deal?'. That the name field outweighs keywords for App Store search is common ASO knowledge, not sourced here.
fix: Name 'Pexi: Grocery Price Checker' (27 chars). Subtitle on the outcome, e.g. 'Scan it, know if it is a deal' (29). Then drop grocery/price/checker from keywords and spend those characters on deals,flyer,sale,cheap,unit,barcode,scan,food,shopping,list.
fix_cost: 20 minutes in App Store Connect (Jamin owns the listing), $0

title: Rank 3. Three screens stand between install and the camera, and the third is a no-choice 'Your data' page that reads as a warning
evidence: app/public/js/onboarding-flow.js:223-225 (onboarding off: permissions, then consent, then camera), after the agree guard (main.js:120, agree.js header). With photoId and onboarding off, consent.js:68 draws no switch, only text: voice.js:1548 'Every scan is written down: the product and the price you saw, always...' and voice.js:1622 '...uses it to answer other shoppers and to train Pexi, and the person running it can see it too.' No ruling found that requires this screen (grep RULINGS.md 'consent', 'your data': only location-once rules at lines 496-509). The agree screen (Terms tick plus the Claude question, Apple 5.1.2) has a named cost and stays.
fix: Remove the 'Your data' screen from the first run (its facts are in the privacy policy linked on the agree screen), so install goes agree, permissions, camera. Optionally word the Claude answers by benefit: 'Yes, get sharper prices' / 'No, use broad guesses'.

title: Rank 4. The paywall tells a shopper how to avoid paying: 'Typing a name is always free'
evidence: app/public/js/ui-strings.js:99 paywall_step_free_d: '10 barcode scans every week. Typing a name is always free.', drawn in the steps list on the plans screen (screens/paywall.js steps, line ~184 'scan' step). RULINGS.md:471-473 makes typed searches free; it does not require the subscribe screen to say so.
fix: Make it '10 barcode scans every week.' Keep 'Type a name instead' on the limit-spent screen only, as the quiet second way out.

title: Rank 5. The paywall sells a count, not a result: 'Pexi Plus: 100 barcode scans a week (free: 10)'
evidence: app/public/js/ui-strings.js:70 paywall_heading; screenshot iphone-6.3/06-paywall.png shows it as the headline over the plans. Plus has no other feature to sell (paywall_step_plus_d, ui-strings.js:101 '100 barcode scans every week.').
fix: Lead with the outcome within hard rule 2 (no savings words): heading like 'Check every price in your cart', the 100-a-week fact underneath. Show the mascot's verdict face, not a bare list.

title: Rank 6. Most of the 10 free scans go on answers with no shop price, so a new shopper hits the wall after about 3 strong answers
evidence: app/src/scan-quota.ts:14-21 and :119-122 count every answered barcode with a name (resolved_label NOT NULL), whatever the answer held. notes/catch-up.md:29 'only 27% of real scans had a shop price' (2026-11-14). 10 x 0.27 = about 3 priced answers before scan 11 is refused. Effect on conversion is not measured.
fix: Count a scan only when its answer had shop prices (scan.verdict_sellers > 0, column at app/src/scans.ts:412). Model cost is small (docs/decisions.md 'Free 10 scans a week, Plus 100': about US$0.0023 per range call). Re-check once the funnel (rank 9) shows real numbers.
fix_cost: 1 to 2 hours server plus a test (Jamin's side), $0

title: Rank 7. The weekly limit is invisible until it refuses a scan at the shelf
evidence: The scans-left line exists only on the You screen (app/public/js/screens/you.js:108, ui-strings.js:117 'N of 10 free scans left this week'). The 11th scan gets a 402 and the camera swaps the answer for the paywall (screens/camera.js:6019-6022). Live: curl /api/quota as probe-review-business answered {"limit":10,"used":0,"remaining":10,"resetsAt":null,"plus":false}, so the wall is on now.
fix: From the 7th scan, add one line on the answer sheet: '3 free scans left this week. Get Plus' opening the paywall. Surprise walls cost ratings; a warned shopper converts at a moment they chose.

title: Rank 8. No free trial at launch; the named cost of a trial is small, the cost of none is unmeasured
evidence: docs/paywall-go-live-2026-11-17.md:40-41 'No free trial on either subscription'. Reason, docs/security-check/legal-review-2026-11-17.md:261-264: Quebec wants a written notice before a trial converts; 'the cost is refunds to Quebec subscribers who complain'. Paywall code already draws a trial when the store reports one (purchases.js:159-190). Uplift from a trial is not measured for Pexi.
fix: Decide with numbers after launch: start without, and switch on a 3-day trial on the yearly plan in App Store Connect if paywall-to-purchase is weak (no code change).
fix_cost: 15 minutes in App Store Connect, $0 plus possible Quebec refunds

title: Rank 9. The funnel can be measured from data already collected, but nothing computes it (adds to R24: no new phone events are needed)
evidence: Events present: app_open (app/public/js/track.js:171), screen_view with previousScreen (track.js:201, covers paywall views and where from), scan_limit_hit (screens/camera.js:6020), paywall_buy with outcome 'done' (screens/paywall.js:412-418), scan rows with verdict_sellers (app/src/scans.ts:412). grep -i 'funnel|cohort|d7' over app/src and scripts found no report. Installs: App Store Connect; revenue: RevenueCat.
fix: One read-only script on the Mac, weekly: devices whose first app_open fell in the week, how many got a scan with verdict_sellers > 0, saw screen 'paywall', reached paywall_buy done, and sent app_open 7 days later. Fold into R24's weekly email.

title: Rank 10. On about 3 in 4 scans the answer opens by saying what Pexi lacks
evidence: app/public/js/ui-strings.js:245 cat_basis_broad 'A broad guess: Pexi has no prices for items like this yet'; :344 vd_prov_claude_typical 'An AI estimate; no shop prices found'; :367 'an AI estimate, no prices for this item'. Share from notes/catch-up.md:29 (27% had a shop price).
fix: Keep the word 'estimate' (an honest label is what makes the range defensible) and drop the apology: 'Pexi's estimate for Canada' / 'Typical price, Pexi's AI estimate'. Add the existing pad line 'add the shelf price and Pexi will know it next time' as the call to act.

title: The store description volunteers doubts before benefits
evidence: docs/store/listing.md:30 'Estimates can be wrong.'; :39 'Coverage is limited, so Pexi cannot answer for every product or every store, and prices change.'; :46 'Prices and estimates are information only.' Few browsers expand the description, so the loss is small.
fix: Open with the outcome (scan, get a verdict in seconds, see the Canadian range and which shops had it); keep the estimate label, the no-affiliation line and the subscription and links paragraph Apple needs (Guideline 3.1.2).

title: Competitors: Pexi's opening is the in-store 'is this price good' question; it loses on ratings, coverage and free rivals
evidence: Flipp https://apps.apple.com/ca/app/flipp-flyers-shopping-deals/id725097967 'Save on Groceries, Food & More', free, 4.7 from 865K ratings, flyers and price matching. Yuka https://apps.apple.com/ca/app/yuka-food-cosmetic-scanner/id1092799236 'Find healthy products', 4.8 from 29K, Premium $20/$25/$30 a year. Canadian Grocery Flyers & Deal https://apps.apple.com/ca/app/canadian-grocery-flyers-deal/id6753903055 3.9 from 22, $3.99 monthly, $7.99 yearly. Price Scanner Barcode https://apps.apple.com/ca/app/price-scanner-barcode/id728175625 4.4 from 517, free with ad-removal $2.99 to $17.99. GroceryChop https://apps.apple.com/ca/app/grocerychop-compare-prices/id6776418172 too few ratings, Premium $9.99. None of these gives a verdict on the shelf price in your hand.
fix: Position against Flipp in the subtitle and first caption: Flipp shows flyers, Pexi checks the price in your hand. Ask for a rating right after a Great verdict (review-prompt.js exists; check its trigger) to get past zero ratings fast.
fix_cost: in the screenshot and name work above

title: Price level is in line with what Canadian shoppers already see; the weak point is what Plus says it gives, not the price
evidence: Pexi CA$3.99 a month, CA$29.99 a year (RULINGS.md:470, docs/store/screenshots/plans.json). Canadian Grocery Flyers & Deal monthly $3.99; Yuka $20 to $30 a year (store pages above). Yearly shows 'about $2.50 a month' (paywall-strings.js:15).
fix: None for price. Revisit after the funnel shows paywall-to-purchase.
